pr_title: Fix `FindProvider` calls on `SkinProvidingContainer` not considering disable flags
pr_body:
Can't find a better way to handle this. Did look at making overloaded `FindProvider` calls but some special cases we use require the predicate function (see https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/2c1f22d7ae914e84a6263d4ae7231d2f0f2a3bb7/osu.Game/Skinning/LegacySkinExtensions.cs#L30-L37).

Closes #13394.
pr_comments: On checking the beatmap linked in the issue, things aren't 100% correct yet (besides the slider ball colour issue). The HP bar and the score counter don't update correctly, but I haven't yet looked in detail as to why.

Nice catch. There was a missing passing of `SourceChanged` through the transformer in the case where the transformer's main source is an `ISkinSource`. Have added this in, but also keep in mind that this flow is likely going to go away with https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/13403.

issue_context.title: Beatmap skin doesn't get completely deactivated when having it set to off
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug:** 
When playing a beatmap that has it's own skin and having beatmap skins disabled, the cursor, moving object on sliders as well as the "connection lines" between hit objects still appear in the beatmaps skin.
**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:** 
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1DLuTEWBd2O9X_KZ6PMK_LqN3uaB7jQo8/view?usp=sharing
First map doesn't has it's own skin (and that's how the skin usually looks), second map has a skin which results in these visual glichtes.
**osu!lazer version:** 
2021.608.0
**Logs:**

comments:
Would be easier if you attached a link to the beatmap, but it's https://osu.ppy.sh/beatmapsets/64525#osu/200670.

Can you please attach the skin you're seeing this issue on as well? if it's not present on all skins.
Well this is likely to be the case on all skins. `FindProvider` is not taking `Allow{Drawable,Texture,Sample}Lookup` into account it seems.
Ah right, that was actually a noticed issue but got forgotten down all the reconsiderations that went inside #13264.

review_comments:
I'm so confused. How does this in any way "pass through the Allow checks"?

```
noFallbackLookupProxy = new NoFallbackProxy(this);

noFallbackLookupProxy.GetTexture(...)
  == provider.GetTexture(..., false)
  == this.GetTexture(..., false)
```
What am I missing?

by "pass through" i mean "run" them.

the critical part of that comment is the following words "without implicitly falling back to the fallbackSource"

in other words, the difference is that the proxy is using the `false` parameter to avoid the fallback logic.
I'm not sure why, but having public methods with the fallback parameter confused me.
Do you think it's worth tidying them up? Moving the interface implementation to implicit and giving `fallback` a default parameter?
Dunno, it's fine for now. Probably makes more sense this way from the consumer's POV.
